Implemented on branch work/claude-retention in standalone clone /private/tmp/eyes4s-claude-retention (base 9431e120), commit 1bb152e0e8f1ed144997e9a32add568237db0bba, tree 468969af1f8d18e88b0f546ab2e58d615f1e8891. Not pushed, not merged.

Policy: after a save's manifest swap AND journal reset succeed, ProjectSession removes every part file (ProjectBundle.isPartFile: <area>/<stem>.<16hex>.json directly in mappings/datasets/analyses/reporting/figures, or runs/<n>/run.<16hex>.json) named by neither the new project.json nor the kept project.previous.json. Never touched: inputs/, runs/<n>/archive/, journals/, cache/, sidecars, lock/staged files. The journal names no part (start line = base document digest; after the reset that is the new manifest's document). Collection is skipped when the reset failed (JournalNotReset) or the previous manifest is unreadable/undecodable; failures and raised store errors are reported in the new SaveReceipt.collection: PartCollection and never fail the save. Docs: ProjectSession class Scaladoc "Part retention", BundleArea, SaveReceipt/PartCollection.

Tests: PartRetentionConformance (9 tests) run as PartRetentionSuite (studio-core JVM+JS, in-memory) and FilePartRetentionSuite (studio-desktop, FileProjectStore, non-FX). Passed: GITHUB_ACTIONS=true sbt studioCoreJVM/Test/compile studioCoreJS/Test/compile studioDesktop/Test/compile; studioCoreJVM+JS testOnly session.* bundle.* runs.* (143 each); studioDesktop testOnly platform.File* runtime.SessionPortSuite (97); scalafmtAll + headerCheckAll on the three projects; studioStyleCheck. No FX suites run.

Mutation (PartRetentionSuite): drop previous-manifest keep set -> 7 fail; collect even when reset failed -> 1 fail; treat undecodable previous as empty -> 1 fail; keep only previous manifest (pre-swap view) -> 8 fail; isPartFile accepts any depth under runs/ -> 4 fail; stop catching raised store errors -> 2 fail. One earlier variant of the depth mutant survived until a part-shaped file inside runs/1/archive/ was planted.

Open for owner: archived journals (journals/archive/*.jsonl) name their base document by digest only; their base parts are not retained once two newer saves exist.
